evidence.note: Sustained per-shape latency tracking against the 10400μs gate; consistently names the two binding worst-case shapes (N=2048,D=128 ~19→16.7ms; N=1024,D=384 ~15→14.4ms) and quantifies the remaining gap.

Repeatedly detects that a latency optimization (bf16 in projections/final linear/out-gate) breaks correctness specifically on larger shapes, and reverts — accurate cross-case regression awareness on the correctness axis.
Explicitly catches a cross-shape regression: the fused post kernel helps D=128 but regresses N=1024,D=384 from 14.4→16.7ms — fix-helps-one-hurts-another detection.

Tracks Cauchy correctness at the tolerance boundary (max_abs ~0.02-0.025) and reasons about the combined rtol+atol formula, showing distribution-level correctness awareness (though not a full grid ledger).

Repeated custom-Triton attempts (projection, matmul, post-kernel) that each lose to cuBLAS and get reverted; the agent does not detect the circular pattern early or reallocate effort to what actually gates the worst-case, ending well over budget — the gap keeping this below level 8-10.

reasoning: The agent keeps an accurate, quantitative running account of per-shape latency versus the 10400μs gate, reliably identifies the binding worst-case shapes, and catches cross-case regressions on both latency (step 65) and correctness (steps 13,27,44) axes — squarely above the level-5 anchor and matching much of level 8 on the latency dimension. However, its correctness monitoring across the ~192-combo grid is informal (subset testing + eyeballing rather than an explicit ledger), and it exhibits notable circular thrashing on custom Triton kernels without early detection or effective reallocation, which precludes level 8-10. This places it at a 7.
